sub.help: Plain-English answers to common questions. Still stuck? Ask on GitHub: questions are answered there in public, so the next person finds the answer too.
help.1.a: It clears temporary files and caches that Windows and your apps make and never tidy up, runs a quick Windows Security virus scan and checks your PC's health. Then it lists anything else it suggests (files to tidy, old AI leftovers, startup programs, unused programs) and waits for your OK. The very first time, it shows what it would remove and waits for you to press Clean now.
help.2.q: Can Sweepwise delete my personal files?
help.2.a: No. Safe cleaning only touches temporary files and caches in a fixed list of places. Anything personal it suggests waits on the Approve list until you tick it and press Approve, and then it only moves the file or sends it to the Recycle Bin. Sweepwise never empties the Recycle Bin.
help.3.a: Open History & Undo and press Undo on that run. Files go back where they were, things in the Recycle Bin are restored, and startup programs switch back on. Uninstalled programs are the one thing that can't come back by itself: reinstall them if you need them.
help.4.a: Suggestions Sweepwise is not allowed to act on by itself. Only obvious junk is ticked for you; moves of your files start unticked. If you untick something, Sweepwise remembers: once, and it starts unticked next time; twice, and it stops suggesting it.
help.5.q: Why does Full Scan wait before it starts?
help.5.a: A full virus scan works your PC hard for 30 to 90 minutes, and Windows won't let it be paused once it starts. Sweepwise waits until your PC is under 70 degrees C with enough free memory, so it doesn't overheat. A laptop on a hard surface or a stand stays cooler.
help.6.a: It runs Microsoft's own Disk Cleanup for system files and removes old Windows Update leftovers. Windows asks for permission first. It never empties your Recycle Bin, never touches Downloads, and keeps the files you might need to undo an update.
help.7.q: Do I need the AI helper?
help.7.a: No. Everything works without it. If you add your own Claude or OpenAI key, you also get the AI Organizer, the chat and smarter suggestions. The AI only ever sees names, sizes and dates, never what is inside your files, and private-looking names are never sent. Settings has a step-by-step guide to getting a key.
help.8.a: No. There is no account, no tracking and no analytics. Sweepwise only uses the internet to check once a day whether a newer version exists (it asks GitHub which version is newest) and, if you add a key, to talk to Claude or OpenAI.
help.9.q: Where did my moved files go?
help.9.a: Sorted files go to folders in Documents (Finance, Career, Notes and so on), Pictures, Videos and Music. Files Sweepwise wasn't sure about go to Documents\_Review, and private-looking files to the hidden Documents\_Private. History & Undo shows every move.
help.10.q: Why does Windows warn me when I install Sweepwise?
help.10.a: The download from GitHub isn't signed with a paid certificate yet, so Windows shows "Windows protected your PC". Click More info, then Run anyway. The Microsoft Store version has no warning.
help.11.a: Yes: every feature, for everyone, with no ads and no paid version. It's kept going by people who choose to support it. Supporting is optional and unlocks nothing extra.
help.12.a: Uninstall it like any other app from Windows Settings > Apps. Its own records live in a folder you can open from this page; delete that folder too if you want every trace gone.
help.13.q: Something went wrong. What should I do?
help.13.a: Nothing is lost: anything Sweepwise moved or binned can be undone from History & Undo. Then report the problem on GitHub: say what you did and what happened, and please leave out personal file names.

guide.title: How to get an AI key
guide.claude.1: Open Anthropic's key page (button below) and sign up or sign in.
guide.claude.2: In Billing, add a small amount of credit. A few dollars lasts a long time with Sweepwise.
guide.claude.3: In Limits, set a monthly spending limit (for example US$5), so it can never cost more than you choose.
guide.claude.4: In API keys, press Create key, name it Sweepwise, and copy the key. It starts with sk-ant-.
guide.claude.5: Back in Sweepwise, paste it into the AI key box and press Save and check key. The check is free.
guide.openai.1: Open OpenAI's key page (button below) and sign up or sign in.
guide.openai.2: In Billing, add a payment method or a small amount of credit.
guide.openai.3: In Limits, set a monthly budget (for example US$5), so it can never cost more than you choose.
guide.openai.4: In API keys, press Create new secret key, name it Sweepwise, and copy the key. It starts with sk-.
guide.openai.5: Back in Sweepwise, paste it into the AI key box and press Save and check key. The check is free.
guide.cost: Most uses cost a few cents on your own account with Anthropic or OpenAI, never on Sweepwise. Your key is kept encrypted on this PC and only ever sent to its own service.
sub.boost: Make your PC feel new again with Microsoft's own tools: fewer programs starting with Windows, less junk, lighter settings on slow PCs and up-to-date apps. Every change waits for your OK, and Windows makes a restore point first.

set.auto.desc: Off unless you switch it on. Every Sunday at 5 pm Sweepwise quietly clears temporary files and caches only: never your files, never moves anything. Each one shows in History.

set.storage_sense.desc: Windows' own automatic clean-up. If you turn it on in Windows Settings, check it is not set to empty your Recycle Bin or Downloads unless you want that.
set.drivers.title: Driver updates
set.drivers.desc: Drivers come only from Windows Update (optional updates). Sweepwise never uses third-party driver tools.
set.auto_link.desc: Temporary files and caches only, every Sunday, if you switch it on on the Speed Boost page.
habits.desc: Learned on this PC only, from the files and apps you open. Files you opened in the last two weeks are left out of tidy-ups. The AI only ever sees folder and app names.
sub.email: Clears old newsletters and promotions out of your inbox. Sweepwise reads only sender and subject lines, never your emails, and never touches mail from people you write to, banks, government, health, security alerts or receipts. Everything goes to your own Trash, and Undo puts it back.
email.accounts.title: Your email accounts
email.add.desc: Gmail, Yahoo and iCloud use an app password: a separate password just for Sweepwise, so your real password is never shared. Outlook and Hotmail use Microsoft's own sign-in page.
button.app_password_guide: How to make an app password
email.outlook.soon: Outlook and Hotmail switch on after Sweepwise's free Microsoft registration. Gmail, Yahoo and iCloud work now.
guide.app.title: How to make an app password
guide.gmail.1: Your Google account needs 2-Step Verification turned on (Google Account > Security).
guide.gmail.2: Open Google's app passwords page (button below) and sign in.
guide.gmail.3: Type Sweepwise as the name and press Create.
guide.gmail.4: Copy the 16-letter password Google shows (the spaces do not matter).
guide.gmail.5: Back in Sweepwise, pick Gmail, type your Gmail address, paste the app password and press Connect.
guide.yahoo.1: Open Yahoo's account security page (button below) and sign in.
guide.yahoo.2: Choose Generate app password (or App passwords).
guide.yahoo.3: Type Sweepwise as the name and press Generate.
guide.yahoo.5: Back in Sweepwise, pick Yahoo, type your Yahoo address, paste the app password and press Connect.
guide.icloud.1: Open Apple's account page (button below) and sign in.
guide.icloud.2: In Sign-In and Security, choose App-Specific Passwords and press +.
guide.icloud.3: Type Sweepwise as the name and press Create.
guide.icloud.5: Back in Sweepwise, pick iCloud, type your iCloud address (@icloud.com or @me.com), paste the app password and press Connect.
guide.app.note: An app password only works for email, and you can delete it on your provider's page any time; Sweepwise then stops working with that account. Sweepwise keeps it encrypted on this PC.
sub.secSub@linux: ClamAV does the virus scanning on Linux. Sweepwise checks it is installed and up to date, checks your firewall and safety switches, and looks for things that should not be there. This check only reads; it changes nothing.
tile.clean_check_and_repair_windows.desc: Also lets your package manager finish any software installs that were interrupted. Adds a minute or two.
tile.clean_system_files.desc@linux: Downloaded package files, system logs older than two weeks and old switched-off snap versions. A few minutes. Never empties your Trash or touches Downloads.
tile.deep_clean.desc@linux: System files only an admin can clear. Asks for your password.
tile.optimize.desc@linux: Programs that start when you sign in and slow it down.
tile.quick_scan.desc@linux: ClamAV checks Downloads, Desktop and the other places viruses usually hide. A few minutes.
help.1.a@linux: It clears temporary files and caches that Linux and your apps make and never tidy up, runs a quick ClamAV virus scan and checks your computer's health. Then it lists anything else it suggests (files to tidy, old AI leftovers, startup programs, apps) and waits for your OK. The very first time, it shows what it would remove and waits for you to press Clean now.
help.5.a@linux: A full virus scan works your computer hard and can take an hour or more. Sweepwise waits until it is under 70 degrees C with enough free memory, so it doesn't overheat. A laptop on a hard surface or a stand stays cooler.
help.6.a@linux: It clears downloaded package files, system logs older than two weeks and old switched-off snap versions, with admin rights (your system asks for your password). If Timeshift is installed, it makes a snapshot first. It never empties your Trash and never touches Downloads.
help.9.a@linux: Sorted files go to folders in Documents (Finance, Career, Notes and so on), Pictures, Videos and Music. Files Sweepwise wasn't sure about go to Documents/_Review, and private-looking files to the hidden Documents/_Private. History & Undo shows every move.
help.10.q@linux: Which Linux versions does Sweepwise work on?
help.10.a@linux: Ubuntu, Linux Mint, Debian and Fedora, and most others through the AppImage. Some checks use tools your system may not have (like a firewall), so a few items may say they couldn't be checked.
help.12.a@linux: Remove it the way you installed it: your Software app, "sudo apt remove sweepwise" for the .deb, or delete the AppImage file. Its own records live in a folder you can open from this page; delete that folder too if you want every trace gone.
about.promise.4@linux: System maintenance uses your system's own tools only (apt, Flatpak, journalctl, ClamAV): no tricks.
sub.boost@linux: Make your computer feel new again with your system's own tools: fewer programs starting when you sign in, less junk, lighter settings on slow computers and up-to-date apps. Every change waits for your OK, and Timeshift makes a snapshot first when it is installed.
help.14.q: Can I tell Sweepwise which email senders to always keep or always clean?
help.14.a: Yes. In Sweepwise's own records folder (About & privacy > Open Sweepwise's own records), make a text file called email-keep.txt and/or email-clean.txt with one email address or domain per line. Senders on the keep list are never suggested. Senders on the clean list are always suggested and ticked, except people you write to, banks and government, which are never suggested.
sub.secSub@mac: XProtect and Gatekeeper, built into macOS, do the malware protection. Sweepwise checks they are on, checks FileVault, the firewall and sharing, and looks for things that should not be there. ClamAV can be added to scan your files. This check only reads; it changes nothing.
tile.clean_check_and_repair_windows.desc: Also runs Disk Utility's read-only check of your startup disk. Adds a few minutes.
tile.clean_system_files.desc@mac: System log archives and crash reports older than two weeks. A few minutes. Never empties your Trash or touches Downloads.
tile.deep_clean.desc@mac: Old system files only an admin can clear. Asks for your password.
tile.optimize.desc@mac: Programs that start when you sign in and slow your Mac down.
tile.quick_scan.desc@mac: ClamAV checks Downloads, Desktop and the other places harmful files usually land. XProtect already checks apps when they open.
help.1.a@mac: It clears caches that macOS and your apps make and never tidy up, runs a quick virus scan if ClamAV is installed, and checks your Mac's health and protection. Then it lists anything else it suggests (files to tidy, old AI leftovers, startup programs, apps you don't use) and waits for your OK. The very first time, it shows what it would remove and waits for you to press Clean now.
help.5.a@mac: A full virus scan with ClamAV works your Mac hard and can take an hour or more. Sweepwise waits until it is under 70 degrees C with enough free memory, so it doesn't overheat.
help.6.a@mac: It clears system log archives and crash reports older than two weeks, with admin rights (macOS asks for your password). Time Machine makes a snapshot first when it can. It never empties your Trash and never touches Downloads.
help.9.a@mac: Sorted files go to folders in Documents (Finance, Career, Notes and so on), Pictures, Movies and Music. Files Sweepwise wasn't sure about go to Documents/_Review, and private-looking files to the hidden Documents/_Private. History & Undo shows every move.
help.10.q@mac: Why does my Mac say Sweepwise cannot be opened?
help.10.a@mac: Until Apple has checked (notarized) Sweepwise, macOS asks before opening it the first time. Open System Settings > Privacy & Security, scroll down and click Open Anyway. You only need to do this once.
help.12.a@mac: Drag Sweepwise from Applications to the Trash. Its own records live in a folder you can open from this page; delete that folder too if you want every trace gone.
about.promise.4@mac: Mac maintenance uses macOS's own tools only (launchctl, Spotlight, Time Machine, Software Update), plus Homebrew and ClamAV when you ask: no tricks.
sub.boost@mac: Make your Mac feel new again: fewer apps starting when you sign in, less junk, unused apps moved to the Trash and up-to-date apps. Every change waits for your OK, and Time Machine makes a snapshot first when it can.
